questions.question: A ball is thrown upward with an initial velocity of 12 m/s. What will be its velocity after 1 second? (Take g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.2 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The motion of the ball follows the **first equation of motion**, which relates final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration, and time.
 
• Given data: The **initial velocity (u)** is **12 m/s**, the **time (t)** is **1 second**, and the **acceleration due to gravity (g)** is **9.8 m/s²**.
 
• When an object is thrown **upward**, it moves against the force of gravity. Therefore, the **acceleration (a)** is taken as **-g**, which is **-9.8 m/s²**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct in its application of sign convention.***
 
• Applying the formula **v = u + at**, we substitute the values: **v = 12 + (-9.8 × 1)**.
 
• The calculation results in **v = 12 - 9.8**, which equals **2.2 m/s**. ***Hence, the final velocity after 1 second is 2.2 m/s.***
 
• Since the resulting **velocity** is positive, it indicates that the ball is **still moving upward** but at a significantly reduced speed due to the constant downward pull of **gravity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Equations of Motion:**

 
 
• These equations describe the behavior of a physical system in terms of its motion as a function of **time**. They are valid only when **acceleration is constant**.
 
• **First Equation:** **v = u + at** (Velocity-Time relation).
 
• **Second Equation:** **s = ut + 1/2 at²** (Position-Time relation), where **s** is **displacement**.
 
• **Third Equation:** **v² = u² + 2as** (Velocity-Position relation).
 
 
 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity (g):**
 
 
• On **Earth**, the standard value for **g** is approximately **9.8 m/s²**. It represents the constant acceleration experienced by an object in **free fall**.
 
• The value of **g** varies slightly depending on the **location** (altitude and latitude), being higher at the **poles** and lower at the **equator**.
 
 
 
• **Sign Convention in Kinematics:**
 
 
• In vertical motion, if we consider the **upward direction** as positive, then **initial velocity (u)** is positive, and **acceleration due to gravity (g)** is negative because it acts **downward**.
 
• At the **maximum height** of the trajectory, the **final velocity (v)** of the object becomes **0 m/s** momentarily before it starts descending.
 
 
 
• **Scalar vs Vector Quantities:**
 
 
• **Velocity** is a **vector quantity**, meaning it has both **magnitude** and **direction**. In this problem, the magnitude is **2.2 m/s** and the direction is **upward**.
 
• **Speed** is a **scalar quantity** and only represents the magnitude of the rate of motion.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• If the **time** given was longer, such as **2 seconds**, the velocity would become **negative** (12 - 19.6 = -7.6 m/s), indicating the ball has already reached its peak and is **falling back down**.
 
• The **maximum height** reached by the ball can be calculated using the formula **s = u² / 2g**. For an initial velocity of **12 m/s**, the maximum height would be approximately **7.35 meters**.
 
• The **total time of flight** for the ball to return to the thrower's hand (ignoring air resistance) is calculated as **T = 2u / g**, which would be approximately **2.45 seconds**.

questions.question: The fluid content inside the plasma membrane, which also contains many specialised cell organelles, is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**cytoplasm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cytoplasm** is the thick, jelly-like fluid content that is enclosed within the **plasma membrane** and surrounds the **nucleus** of a cell.
 
• It serves as the primary arena for most **metabolic activities** and chemical reactions necessary for life, such as **glycolysis** (the initial stage of cellular respiration).
 
• The cytoplasm is not just a simple fluid; it contains many **specialised cell organelles** like **mitochondria**, **endoplasmic reticulum**, **ribosomes**, and the **Golgi apparatus**, each performing a specific **function** for the cell.
 
• The portion of the cytoplasm that is not occupied by organelles is called the **cytosol**, which consists mainly of **water** (about **70% to 90%**), **salts**, and **organic molecules** like proteins and enzymes.
 
• It plays a vital role in **structural support**, maintaining the shape of the cell, and facilitates the movement of materials via **cytoplasmic streaming**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nucleoplasm:**

 
 
• Also known as **karyoplasm**, this is the highly gelatinous fluid found inside the **nucleus** of eukaryotic cells.
 
• It provides the medium in which the **nucleolus** and **chromatin** (containing DNA) are suspended.
 
• The **nuclear envelope** acts as a barrier that separates the **nucleoplasm** from the **cytoplasm**, allowing for controlled transport of molecules through **nuclear pores**.
 
 
 
• **Vacuoplasm (Cell Sap):**
 
 
• This refers to the fluid found inside a **vacuole**, a storage **organelle** particularly prominent and large in **plant cells**.
 
• It contains various substances such as **water**, **sugars**, **salts**, **amino acids**, and sometimes **metabolic waste** products.
 
• In plants, it helps maintain **turgor pressure**, which provides the cell with **rigidity** and structural integrity.
 
 
 
• **Plasmin:**
 
 
• Unlike the other terms, **plasmin** is not a part of the internal cell structure; it is an important **proteolytic enzyme** present in the **blood**.
 
• Its primary **function** is to degrade **fibrin clots**, a process known as **fibrinolysis**, which prevents blood clots from becoming too large and causing health issues.
 
• It is derived from its inactive precursor, **plasminogen**, which is produced in the **liver**.
 
 
 
• **Protoplasm:**
 
 
• The term **protoplasm** refers to the entire living substance of the cell, including both the **cytoplasm** and the **nucleus**.
 
• It was first coined by the scientist **J.E. Purkinje** in **1839** to describe the physical basis of life within a cell.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Plasma Membrane:** This is a **selectively permeable** membrane that regulates the entry and exit of molecules, thereby protecting the **internal environment** of the cytoplasm.
 
• **Cell Organelles:** These are **membrane-bound** structures within the cytoplasm. For example, **mitochondria** are the **powerhouse** of the cell because they generate **ATP** (Adenosine Triphosphate), the **energy currency** of the cell.
 
• **Eukaryotic vs. Prokaryotic:** In **eukaryotic cells** (like those in humans and plants), the cytoplasm contains complex organelles, whereas in **prokaryotic cells** (like bacteria), there are no membrane-bound organelles, and the **genetic material** is suspended directly in the cytoplasm.

questions.question: A force F acts on a body of mass m producing acceleration a . If the force is 3 F and mass of the body is reduced to m/2 . What is the value of new acceleration in terms of 'a'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6 a**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion** provides the fundamental relationship between **force**, **mass**, and **acceleration**. It states that the **acceleration** of an object is directly proportional to the net **force** acting on it and inversely proportional to its **mass**.
 
• The mathematical expression for this law is **F = m × a**, where **F** is the **force** applied, **m** is the **mass** of the body, and **a** is the **acceleration** produced. From this, the **acceleration** can be derived as **a = F / m**.
 
• In the first scenario provided in the question, the **force** is **F** and the **mass** is **m**, which results in an **acceleration** of **a = F / m**.
 
• In the second scenario, the **force** is increased to **3F** and the **mass** is reduced to **m/2**. To find the **new acceleration (a')**, we substitute these new values into the formula: **a' = (3F) / (m / 2)**.
 
• By performing the algebraic calculation, **a' = 3F × (2 / m)**, which simplifies to **a' = 6 × (F / m)**. Since the original **acceleration a** is **F / m**, the new value becomes **a' = 6a**.
 
• This demonstrates that increasing the **force** while simultaneously decreasing the **mass** leads to a significantly higher **acceleration**. *Hence, the statement that the new acceleration is 6a is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Force (F):** It is an external agency capable of changing the state of rest or motion of a particular body. It is a **vector quantity**, meaning it has both **magnitude** and **direction**. The **SI unit** of **force** is the **Newton (N)**, which is equivalent to **1 kg·m/s²**.
 
• **Mass (m):** This represents the quantity of **matter** contained in a body and serves as a measure of the body's **inertia**. Unlike weight, **mass** is a **scalar quantity** and remains constant regardless of the body's **location** in the universe. Its **SI unit** is the **kilogram (kg)**.
 
• **Acceleration (a):** It is defined as the **rate of change of velocity** with respect to **time**. If the **velocity** of an object changes, it is said to be accelerating. The **SI unit** for **acceleration** is **meters per second squared (m/s²)**.
 
• **Newton's Laws of Motion:** These **three laws** were first compiled by **Sir Isaac Newton** in his work **Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica**, published in **1687**. These laws form the basis for **classical mechanics** and describe the **physics** of moving objects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Inertia and Mass:** The **mass** of an object is a direct measure of its **inertia**. A larger **mass** requires more **force** to achieve the same **acceleration**. In this problem, reducing the **mass** to **m/2** effectively halved the resistance to change in motion, contributing to the increase in **acceleration**.
 
• **Proportionality:** The relationship shows that if **mass** is kept **constant**, **acceleration** is **doubled** when **force** is **doubled**. However, if **force** is kept **constant** and **mass** is **halved**, the **acceleration** also **doubles**. When both changes occur simultaneously as per the question (**3** times the **force** and **1/2** the **mass**), the total effect is **3 × 2 = 6**.
 
• **Practical Applications:** This principle is used in **automotive engineering** to design faster cars by either increasing **engine force (horsepower)** or using lightweight **materials** like **carbon fiber** to reduce the **mass** of the vehicle.

questions.question:
Select the correct option with respect to the following statements.

Statement-1: Suspension is a homogeneous mixture.

Statement-2: The particles of a suspension can be seen by the naked eye.

Statement-3: The solute particles settle down when a suspension is left undisturbed, that is, a suspension is unstable.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Statement 2 and 3 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1** claims that a **suspension** is a **homogeneous mixture**. In reality, a **suspension** is a **heterogeneous mixture** in which the **solute particles** do not dissolve but remain suspended throughout the bulk of the medium. In a **homogeneous mixture**, such as a **true solution**, the composition is uniform throughout. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 2** mentions that the particles of a **suspension** can be seen by the **naked eye**. This is due to the relatively large size of the particles, which are typically larger than **1000 nanometers** (or **1 micrometer**) in diameter. Unlike **colloids** or **true solutions**, where particles are too small to be seen without magnification, **suspension particles** are large enough to scatter **visible light**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 3** states that the **solute particles** settle down when a **suspension** is left **undisturbed**, meaning the **suspension** is **unstable**. Because the particles are large and heavy, the force of **gravity** eventually overcomes the kinetic energy keeping them dispersed, leading to **sedimentation**. Once the particles settle at the bottom, the mixture no longer scatters light as effectively. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The **physical state** of a **suspension** can be altered through **filtration**. Since the particles are larger than the pores of **filter paper**, they can be easily separated from the **solvent** or **dispersion medium**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Properties of Suspensions:**

 
 
• A **suspension** is **heterogeneous** in nature, meaning its components are not distributed uniformly.
 
• The particles scatter a **beam of light** passing through it and make its path **visible**; this phenomenon is known as the **Tyndall Effect**. However, the **Tyndall Effect** disappears once the particles have settled down.
 
• **Examples** of suspensions include **muddy water**, **chalk powder in water**, **flour in water**, and **milk of magnesia**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Mixtures:**
 
 
• **True Solution:** It is a **homogeneous mixture** with a particle size less than **1 nm**. These particles do not scatter light and cannot be seen by the **naked eye**. They are highly **stable** and do not settle.
 
• **Colloid:** It is a **heterogeneous mixture** that appears **homogeneous**. Particle sizes range between **1 nm and 1000 nm**. They show the **Tyndall Effect** but do not settle down, making them **stable**.
 
 
 
• **Applications and Facts:**
 
 
• In the **pharmaceutical industry**, many medicines are prepared as **suspensions** (e.g., antacids) and must be shaken well before **use** to redistribute the settled **solute particles**.
 
• The **instability** of a **suspension** is a key characteristic used in **water treatment plants**, where **coagulants** are added to help suspended impurities settle faster through **sedimentation**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Particle Size:** The defining **feature** of a **suspension** is a particle size greater than **10^-6 meters**.
 
• **Separation:** Unlike **colloids**, which require **centrifugation**, **suspensions** can be separated by simple **mechanical filtration**.
 
• **Optical Properties:** An active **suspension** is **opaque** or **translucent**, but the **supernatant liquid** may become **transparent** once the particles settle.

questions.question: Which of the following plant tissues allows the movement of materials in both directions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phloem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Phloem** is a **complex permanent tissue** in vascular plants that acts as a conduction system for **organic nutrients**, primarily **sucrose**, produced during **photosynthesis**.
 
• Unlike **Xylem**, which only transports water upwards, the movement of materials in the **Phloem** is **bidirectional**. This means it can transport food materials both **upwards and downwards** depending on the plant's requirements.
 
• The process of transporting food materials through the phloem is known as **translocation**. This process is **active** and requires energy in the form of **ATP** to move substances against a concentration gradient.
 
• **Phloem** consists of four main types of cells: **sieve tubes**, **companion cells**, **phloem parenchyma**, and **phloem fibres**. Out of these, only **phloem fibres** are **dead cells**, while the rest are **living tissues**.
 
• The **bidirectional** flow is essential because it allows the **leaves** (the **source**) to send sugar to the **roots** for storage, and during **spring**, it allows the storage organs (the **sink**) to send energy back up to the **developing buds**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Xylem:**

 
 
• It is responsible for the transport of **water and minerals** from the **roots** to the **leaves**.
 
• The flow of materials in the xylem is **unidirectional** (only upwards).
 
• It provides **mechanical strength** to the plant and is composed of **tracheids**, **vessels**, **xylem parenchyma**, and **xylem fibres**.
 
 
 
• **Sclerenchyma:**
 
 
• This is a **simple permanent tissue** made of **dead cells** with extremely **thickened cell walls** containing **lignin**.
 
• Its primary function is to provide **structural support** and **rigidity** to the plant. It is commonly found in **stems**, **veins of leaves**, and the **hard coverings of seeds** and nuts.
 
 
 
• **Fibres:**
 
 
• **Fibres** are a type of **sclerenchyma** cell. They are **elongated**, **tapering**, and have thick **lignified** walls.
 
• In the **commercial** world, fibres from plants like **jute**, **flax**, and **hemp** are used to make **ropes** and **textiles** due to their high **tensile strength**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mechanism of Transport:** The movement in phloem is explained by the **Pressure Flow Hypothesis** (or Mass Flow Hypothesis), where high **osmotic pressure** in the leaves forces the **phloem sap** toward regions of low pressure (the **sink**).
 
• **Vascular Bundles:** Both **Xylem** and **Phloem** together constitute the **vascular bundles** of the plant, which are the main **conducting tissues**.
 
• **Location:** In a typical **dicot stem**, the **Phloem** is usually located towards the **outer side** of the vascular bundle, while the **Xylem** is located towards the **inner side** (pith).
 
• **Sieve Tubes and Companion Cells:** These are uniquely paired. **Sieve tubes** lack a **nucleus** at maturity, so their **metabolic activities** are controlled by the nucleus of the adjacent **companion cells**.

questions.question: An object is placed 30 cm from a concave mirror of focal length 20 cm. Using the mirror formula, what will be the image distance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**-60 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **mirror formula** provides a quantitative relationship between the **object distance (u)**, the **image distance (v)**, and the **focal length (f)** of a spherical mirror. The formula is expressed as **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**.
 
• For a **concave mirror**, the **focal length (f)** is always considered **negative** according to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**. In this problem, the given focal length is **20 cm**, so we use **f = -20 cm**.
 
• The **object distance (u)** is the distance from the **pole** of the mirror to the object. Since the object is placed in front of the mirror, the distance is measured against the direction of incident light, making it **negative**. Here, **u = -30 cm**.
 
• To find the **image distance (v)**, we rearrange the mirror formula: **1/v = 1/f - 1/u**. Substituting the values: **1/v = 1/(-20) - 1/(-30)**.
 
• This simplifies to **1/v = -1/20 + 1/30**. By taking the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of **20 and 30**, which is **60**, the equation becomes **1/v = (-3 + 2) / 60**.
 
• Solving further, **1/v = -1/60**, which gives the result **v = -60 cm**. ***Hence, the image distance is -60 cm and the correct option is -60 cm.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of the Image:** Since the **image distance (v)** is **negative**, the image is formed in front of the mirror. This indicates that the image is **real and inverted**.
 
• **Magnification (m):** Magnification is defined as the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object, also given by **m = -v/u**. In this case, **m = -(-60) / (-30)**, which equals **-2**. A magnification of **-2** means the image is **magnified** (twice the size of the object) and **inverted**.
 
• **Position relative to Center of Curvature:** The **Radius of Curvature (R)** of this mirror is **R = 2f = 40 cm**. Since the object is placed at **30 cm** (between the **Focus at 20 cm** and the **Center of Curvature at 40 cm**), the image must form **beyond the Center of Curvature** (greater than **40 cm**). Our result of **60 cm** aligns with this optical principle.
 
• **Concave Mirror Characteristics:** Often called a **converging mirror**, it has the ability to produce **real** as well as **virtual** images depending on the object's position relative to the **focal point**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sign Convention Rules:** Distances measured in the direction of **incident light** are taken as **positive**, while those measured in the opposite direction are **negative**. All distances are measured from the **pole (P)** of the mirror.
 
• **Focal Lengths:** It is a **fact** that the **focal length** of a **concave mirror** is always **negative**, whereas the focal length of a **convex mirror** is always **positive**.
 
• **Real vs Virtual:** A **positive image distance (v)** for a mirror would imply a **virtual image** formed behind the mirror, while a **negative image distance** signifies a **real image**.
 
• **Practical Uses:** Concave mirrors are utilized in **torches**, **search-lights**, and **vehicle headlights** to get powerful parallel beams of light, as well as by **dentists** to see larger images of teeth.

questions.question: Three resistors of 12 Ω, 6 Ω and 4 Ω are connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance is ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 Ω**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When **resistors** are connected in **parallel**, the reciprocal of the **equivalent resistance** (Req) is the sum of the reciprocals of the **individual resistances**. The formula is given by: **1/Req = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3**.
 
• In this problem, the three resistors are **12 Ω**, **6 Ω**, and **4 Ω**. Substituting these values into the formula: **1/Req = 1/12 + 1/6 + 1/4**.
 
• To solve the fractions, find a **common denominator**, which is **12**. The equation becomes: **1/Req = 1/12 + 2/12 + 3/12**.
 
• Adding the numerators gives: **1/Req = 6/12**. Simplifying this fraction, we get **1/Req = 1/2**.
 
• Taking the reciprocal of both sides, the **equivalent resistance (Req)** is **2 Ω**. ***Hence, the calculated result matches the fourth option.***
 
• A fundamental characteristic of **parallel circuits** is that the **equivalent resistance** is always **less than the smallest individual resistor** in the combination (in this case, 2 Ω is less than 4 Ω).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Parallel Combination of Resistors:**

 
 
• In a **parallel circuit**, the **voltage** across each resistor remains the **same** and is equal to the total voltage of the source.
 
• The total **current** in the circuit is the **sum of the currents** passing through each individual branch.
 
• This type of connection is commonly used in **household wiring** so that each appliance can operate independently at the same voltage.
 
 
 
• **Series Combination of Resistors:**
 
 
• When resistors are connected in **series**, the **total resistance** is the simple sum of individual resistances: **R = R1 + R2 + R3**.
 
• In a series circuit, the **current** remains **constant** through all components, while the **voltage** is divided among them.
 
• If the given resistors (12 Ω, 6 Ω, and 4 Ω) were in series, the **equivalent resistance** would be **22 Ω**.
 
 
 
• **Electrical Resistance:**
 
 
• **Resistance** is the property of a conductor to **oppose the flow of electric current**.
 
• The **SI unit** of resistance is the **Ohm (Ω)**, named after the German physicist **Georg Simon Ohm**.
 
• Factors affecting resistance include the **length** of the conductor, its **cross-sectional area**, the **nature of the material**, and its **temperature**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ohm's Law:** This law states that the **potential difference (V)** across a conductor is **directly proportional** to the **current (I)** flowing through it, provided physical conditions remain constant. The relation is **V = IR**.
 
• **Conductance:** The reciprocal of resistance is called **conductance (G)**, and its **SI unit** is **Siemens (S)** or **mho**. In parallel circuits, the total conductance is the sum of individual conductances (G_total = G1 + G2 + G3).
 
• **Power Dissipation:** In a parallel circuit, the resistor with the **lowest resistance** dissipates the **highest power** because P = V²/R, and V is constant for all.
 
• **Practical Application:** If one component in a **parallel network** fails or is switched off, the **other components continue to function**, which is not the case in a series circuit.

questions.question: A straight chain of three carbon atoms having no double bond and -OH functional group at first carbon atom is named:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Propanol**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The name of an organic compound is determined by the number of **carbon atoms** in its longest chain. A chain with **three carbon atoms** uses the prefix **Prop-**.
 
• The description "having no double bond" indicates that the compound is **saturated**. In chemical nomenclature, saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) use the primary suffix **-ane**. When a functional group is added, the 'e' is typically dropped, making the base name **Propan-**.
 
• The presence of an **-OH functional group** identifies the molecule as an **alcohol**. According to **IUPAC nomenclature**, alcohols are designated by the suffix **-ol**.
 
• The location of the functional group is specified by numbering the carbon chain. Since the **hydroxyl group (-OH)** is at the **first carbon atom**, the systematic name is **Propan-1-ol**, commonly referred to as **Propanol**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Propanol.***
 
• **Evaluating other options:**
 
 
• **Propanone**: This is a **ketone** (suffix **-one**) which requires a **carbonyl group (C=O)** on a non-terminal carbon. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **Propane**: This is a simple **alkane** consisting only of carbon and hydrogen with no functional groups like **-OH**. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **Propanal**: This is an **aldehyde** (suffix **-al**) which contains a **-CHO group** at the end of the chain rather than an **-OH group**. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **IUPAC Nomenclature System**: This is a globally recognized method of naming organic chemical compounds maintained by the **International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry**. It ensures that every compound has a unique and unambiguous name based on its **molecular structure**.
 
• **Root Word Selection**: The prefix is determined by the number of carbons: **Meth- (1)**, **Eth- (2)**, **Prop- (3)**, **But- (4)**, **Pent- (5)**, and **Hex- (6)**. For this question, **three carbons** lead directly to **Prop-**.
 
• **Functional Group Suffixes**:
 
 
• **Alcohols (-OH)**: Use the suffix **-ol**. Example: **Methanol** (CH3OH).
 
• **Aldehydes (-CHO)**: Use the suffix **-al**. Example: **Ethanal** (CH3CHO).
 
• **Ketones (>C=O)**: Use the suffix **-one**. Example: **Butanone** (CH3COCH2CH3).
 
• **Carboxylic Acids (-COOH)**: Use the suffix **-oic acid**. Example: **Ethanoic acid** (CH3COOH).
 
 
 
• **Saturated vs. Unsaturated**: A **saturated** compound contains only **single bonds** between carbon atoms, whereas **unsaturated** compounds contain at least one **double bond** (alkenes, suffix **-ene**) or **triple bond** (alkynes, suffix **-yne**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Structure of Propanol**: The chemical formula for **Propan-1-ol** is **C3H8O**, often written as **CH3CH2CH2OH** to show the straight-chain structure.
 
• **Isomerism**: Propanol has a structural isomer called **Propan-2-ol** (commonly known as **Isopropyl alcohol** or **Isopropanol**), where the **-OH group** is attached to the **second carbon atom** instead of the first.
 
• **Physical Properties**: **Propan-1-ol** is a colorless liquid at **room temperature** and is used extensively as a **solvent** in the pharmaceutical industry and for making **antiseptics**.
 
• **Classification**: It is classified as a **primary alcohol** because the carbon atom holding the **hydroxyl group** is attached to only **one other carbon atom**.

questions.question:
Match the following nature and role of metallic oxides.

 

 
 

 **Column A (Substance)**
 **Column B (Role in Reaction)**
 
 

 <span s
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A - 3; B - 2; C - 1; D - 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **CuO (Copper Oxide)**: Most **metallic oxides** are **basic** in nature. **Copper(II) oxide** reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to produce a salt and water, acting as a base. In the given reaction, it serves as the **basic oxide reacting with acid**. ***Hence, A is matched with 3.***
 
• **HCl (Hydrochloric Acid)**: This is a strong **mineral acid**. In this specific chemical interaction, it acts as the **acid reacting with basic oxide** (CuO) to neutralize the base. ***Hence, B is matched with 2.***
 
• **CuCl2 (Copper Chloride)**: When an acid reacts with a metallic oxide, the resulting compound formed by the replacement of the hydrogen of the acid by a metal is a **salt**. **Copper(II) chloride** is the **salt formed in the reaction**, which gives the solution a characteristic **blue-green color**. ***Hence, C is matched with 1.***
 
• **H2O (Water)**: In a **neutralization reaction** between a base (or basic oxide) and an acid, **water** is always produced alongside the salt. It is considered the **neutralization product** in this context. ***Hence, D is matched with 4.***
 
• The overall chemical equation for this process is: **CuO + 2HCl → CuCl2 + H2O**. This demonstrates the typical behavior of **metal oxides** reacting with **acids**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Oxides**:

 
 
• **Basic Oxides**: These are oxides of metals (like **Na2O**, **MgO**, **CaO**, and **CuO**) that react with acids to form salt and water.
 
• **Acidic Oxides**: These are typically oxides of **non-metals** (like **CO2**, **SO2**, **P2O5**) that react with bases to form salt and water.
 
• **Amphoteric Oxides**: Some metallic oxides, such as **Aluminium oxide (Al2O3)** and **Zinc oxide (ZnO)**, show both acidic and basic behaviors.
 
 
 
• **Neutralization Reaction**: It is a chemical reaction in which an acid and a base react quantitatively with each other. In a reaction in water, neutralization results in there being no excess of **hydrogen ions** or **hydroxide ions** present in the solution.
 
• **Copper(II) Oxide (CuO)**: It is a **black solid**. When it reacts with **HCl**, the black color disappears as it dissolves to form the **blue-green** solution of **Copper(II) chloride**.
 
• **Indicators**: The change in the nature of the solution (from acidic to neutral) during such reactions can often be monitored using **pH indicators** or **litmus paper**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reaction Observation**: During the reaction of **CuO** with **HCl**, the observation of the **color change** is a key identifier of the formation of **CuCl2**. This is a common laboratory experiment to demonstrate the **basic nature** of metallic oxides.
 
• **Valency**: In **Copper(II) oxide**, the **valency of copper** is **+2**. This is why it requires two molecules of **HCl** (each providing one Cl- ion) to form one molecule of **CuCl2**.
 
• **Safety**: Handling **concentrated HCl** requires care due to its **corrosive nature**. Reactions involving metallic oxides and acids are generally **exothermic**, meaning they release heat.
 
• **Solubility**: While **CuO** is **insoluble in water**, it dissolves in acids, which is a characteristic property of basic oxides that are not **alkalis** (water-soluble bases).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a marine fish?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rohu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rohu** (**Labeo rohita**) is a species of fish of the **carp family** (**Cyprinidae**) found in **freshwater** rivers in **South Asia**.
 
• It is a large **omnivore** and is used extensively in **aquaculture** in countries like **India**, **Bangladesh**, **Nepal**, and **Pakistan**. ***Hence, it is not a marine fish.***
 
• It belongs to the category of **Indian Major Carps**, which also includes other freshwater species like **Catla** and **Mrigal**.
 
• **Pomfret** is a **marine fish** found in the **Indo-Pacific** region and is widely consumed in the coastal regions of **India**. ***Hence, statement 1 describes a marine fish.***
 
• **Mackerel** is a common name applied to a number of different species of **pelagic marine fish**, mostly from the family **Scombridae**. ***Hence, statement 4 describes a marine fish.***
 
• **Bhetki**, also known as **Barramundi**, is a **euryhaline** species (can tolerate various salinities) but is primarily found in **estuaries**, **backwaters**, and **marine** coastal waters. ***Hence, it is considered a marine/estuarine fish.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Marine Fisheries:**

 
 
• These involve the exploitation of fish resources from **saltwater** bodies such as **oceans** and **seas**.
 
• In **India**, the marine fishery resources are spread along the **8,118 km** long coastline.
 
• Important marine fish varieties include **Hilsa**, **Sardines**, **Tuna**, **Mackerel**, and **Pomfret**.
 
• The **exclusive economic zone (EEZ)** of India provides a vast area for **deep-sea fishing** operations.
 
 
 
• **Inland Fisheries:**
 
 
• This refers to the catching and farming of fish in **freshwater** resources like **canals**, **ponds**, **reservoirs**, and **rivers**.
 
• **Rohu** is the most important among the **three Indian major carp** species used in polyculture systems.
 
• **Freshwater aquaculture** contributes to a significant portion of the total fish production in **India**, with states like **Andhra Pradesh** and **West Bengal** leading the sector.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Rohu:**
 
 
• **Age and Growth:** It can reach a **maximum length** of about **2 meters** and can live for several years under optimal conditions.
 
• **Features:** It has **cycloid scales**, a **depressed snout**, and is typically **bluish-grey** or **black** on the back with a **silvery-white** belly.
 
• **Diet:** It is mainly a **column feeder**, consuming **phytoplankton** and **decaying organic matter**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Distinction based on Salinity:**

 
 
• **Marine fish** are adapted to high **salinity** levels and possess specialized **osmoregulation** mechanisms to prevent dehydration.
 
• **Freshwater fish** like **Rohu** are adapted to low-salinity environments; placing them in **seawater** would lead to fatal **osmotic shock**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Significance:**
 
 
• The **Blue Revolution** in **India** aimed to increase fish production and productivity from both **marine** and **inland** sources.
 
• **Mackerel** and **Pomfret** are high-value **export** items, contributing significantly to India's **foreign exchange** earnings.
 
• **Rohu** remains the primary source of **animal protein** for a large section of the population in **North** and **East India**.

questions.question:
Read the given statements and select the most appropriate option.

Statement 1: Mirror formula is applicable to both concave and convex mirrors, provided the sign convention is followed.

Statement 2: The validity of Mirror formula depends on the size of the object.

options.text: Both the statements 1 and 2 are correct.
Both the statements 1 and 2 are not correct.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only statement 1 is correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mirror Formula** is a mathematical relationship that connects the **focal length (f)**, the **distance of the object (u)** from the pole, and the **distance of the image (v)** from the pole. The formula is expressed as **1/v + 1/u = 1/f**.
 
• **Statement 1**: This formula is universally applicable to all **spherical mirrors**, which includes both **concave mirrors** and **convex mirrors**. To obtain accurate results for different positions of the object, one must strictly follow the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, where the pole is treated as the origin. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 2**: The derivation of the mirror formula assumes that the **aperture** of the mirror is small compared to its **radius of curvature** and that the rays of light are **paraxial** (rays that make small angles with the principal axis). However, the validity of the formula itself does not depend on the **size of the object**. The object height affects the **magnification**, but the relationship between the distances (u, v, and f) remains constant regardless of how large or small the object is. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Sign Convention** is crucial: distances measured in the direction of **incident light** are taken as positive, while those measured opposite to the direction of incident light are negative. For instance, the **object distance (u)** is almost always **negative** in standard problems.
 
• The **focal length (f)** for a **concave mirror** is always **negative**, whereas for a **convex mirror**, it is always **positive** according to the standard convention.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concave Mirror:**

 
 
• A **concave mirror** is a **converging mirror** that can form both **real and virtual images** depending on the position of the object.
 
• When the object is placed between the **focus (F)** and the **pole (P)**, it forms a **virtual, erect, and magnified** image.
 
• In all other positions beyond the focus, it forms **real and inverted** images of varying sizes.
 
 
 
• **Convex Mirror:**
 
 
• A **convex mirror** is a **diverging mirror** that always forms a **virtual, erect, and diminished** image, regardless of the object's distance from the mirror.
 
• Because it provides a **wider field of view**, it is commonly used as a **rear-view mirror** in vehicles.
 
 
 
• **Linear Magnification (m):**
 
 
• This is defined as the ratio of the **height of the image (h')** to the **height of the object (h)**.
 
• It is also related to distances as **m = -v/u**. A **negative magnification** indicates a **real image**, while a **positive magnification** indicates a **virtual image**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The relationship between the **radius of curvature (R)** and the **focal length (f)** is given by **R = 2f**. This relation holds true for all spherical mirrors with **small apertures**.
 
• In a **concave mirror**, the image is **real** when **v** is negative and **virtual** when **v** is positive.
 
• In a **convex mirror**, the image is always formed behind the mirror, so **v** is always **positive**, and since **u** is **negative**, the magnification **m** is always **positive** and less than **1**.
 
• The **Mirror Formula** was first derived using the principles of **Euclidean geometry** and the **laws of reflection** (Angle of Incidence = Angle of Reflection).

questions.question: Liquids are less compressible because:

options.text: their density is always less than solids

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**particles have moderate gaps**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Compressibility** is the measure of the relative volume change of a fluid or solid as a response to a **pressure** change. In the case of **liquids**, the particles are packed relatively close to each other, meaning the **intermolecular spaces** are much smaller than those in **gases**.
 
• Liquids have **particles that have moderate gaps** compared to gases. While these particles can slide past one another (giving liquids their fluid property), they are close enough that there is very little "empty" space to be squeezed out when pressure is applied. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• The presence of **dissolved gases** in a liquid might slightly increase its overall compressibility or lead to bubble formation under pressure changes, but it is not the primary reason why the liquid state itself is less compressible. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• While the **density** of most liquids is indeed less than that of their solid counterparts (with **water** and **ice** being a notable exception), density is a measure of mass per unit volume, not the mechanism of compression. Compressibility is determined by the availability of space between particles to be reduced. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• All matter in a closed system has a **fixed mass** according to the **Law of Conservation of Mass**. Having a fixed mass is a universal property of matter and does not explain why one state of matter (liquid) resists volume changes more effectively than another (gas). ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **States of Matter and Spacing:**

 
 
• **Solids**: Particles are tightly packed in a regular pattern with negligible **intermolecular spaces**. They are considered **incompressible** for most practical purposes.
 
• **Liquids**: Particles are close together with **moderate gaps** and no regular arrangement. They take the shape of the container but maintain a **fixed volume**.
 
• **Gases**: Particles have very **large gaps** between them and move randomly at high speeds. Because of these vast spaces, gases are **highly compressible**.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Molecular Theory:**
 
 
• This theory states that the distance between **liquid particles** is small enough that **intermolecular attractive forces** (like **Van der Waals forces** or **Hydrogen bonding**) hold them together, preventing the significant volume reduction seen in gases.
 
 
 
• **Bulk Modulus:**
 
 
• The resistance of a substance to compression is quantified by the **Bulk Modulus**. A high Bulk Modulus indicates that a substance is difficult to compress. **Liquids** like **water** have a very high Bulk Modulus (approximately **2.2 GPa**), making them nearly incompressible in hydraulic systems.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• The low compressibility of liquids is the fundamental principle behind **Hydraulic Machinery** (like **Pascal's Law**). Since liquids do not compress easily, pressure applied at one point is transmitted efficiently throughout the fluid to perform work, such as in **car brakes** or **industrial lifts**.

questions.question: When thrown in soil, which of the following substances will persist in the environment for a long time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Broken glass pieces**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Broken glass pieces** are categorized as **non-biodegradable** waste. This means they cannot be broken down or decomposed by the action of **microorganisms** like bacteria, fungi, or earthworms. ***Hence, option 2 is correct.***
 
• **Mango seeds** are organic matter derived from living organisms. They are **biodegradable** and will eventually rot and decompose into the soil, though they take slightly longer than soft tissues due to their hard shell. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Pieces of bread** consist of organic compounds like **carbohydrates**. They are highly **biodegradable** and are quickly decomposed by **molds** and bacteria when exposed to moisture in the soil. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Apple peels** are typical kitchen waste and are **biodegradable**. They decompose rapidly (usually within **few weeks**) and turn into **compost**, adding nutrients back to the environment. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• **Persistence in the environment** refers to the duration a substance remains in the soil without changing its chemical structure. **Glass** is made primarily of **silica (Silicon Dioxide)**, which is extremely stable and can persist for **1 million years** or more.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Biodegradable Substances:**

 
 
• These are substances that are degraded by **natural processes** into simpler, non-toxic substances.
 
• Examples include **agricultural residues**, **paper**, **wood**, **cloth**, and **animal dung**.
 
• The decomposition process is carried out by **decomposers**, which recycle nutrients back into the **ecosystem**.
 
 
 
• **Non-biodegradable Substances:**
 
 
• These substances do not degrade or take a **very long time** (hundreds to thousands of years) to break down.
 
• Common examples include **plastics**, **polythene bags**, **synthetic fibers**, **metal cans**, and **radioactive waste**.
 
• They often act as **pollutants** and can enter the **food chain**, leading to **biological magnification**.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact of Glass:**
 
 
• While **glass** is chemically **inert** and does not leach toxic chemicals like some plastics, its physical presence causes **land pollution**.
 
• In soil, **broken glass** poses a physical hazard to **macro-fauna** such as earthworms and can hinder the **penetration of plant roots**.
 
• Because it does not **oxidize** or **corrode** easily, it remains unchanged in the **geological strata** for eras.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Microbial Enzymes:** Microorganisms produce specific **enzymes** to break down organic bonds (like C-C or C-H bonds in food). However, they do not possess enzymes to break the **silicon-oxygen** bonds found in **glass**.
 
• **Waste Management:** To prevent environmental accumulation, **non-biodegradable** items like **glass** and **metals** should be **recycled**. Glass is **100% recyclable** and can be melted and reformed infinitely without loss in quality.
 
• **Decomposition Timeframes:** While an **apple peel** takes about **2 to 4 weeks** to disappear, a **plastic bottle** may take **450 years**, and **glass** effectively never disappears under normal environmental conditions.

• The **resistance** of a conductor is defined by the formula **R = ρ (l / A)**, where **ρ** is the **resistivity** of the material, **l** is the **length**, and **A** is the **cross-sectional area**.

__
 
• **Factors Affecting Resistance:**

 
 
• **Length (l):** The **resistance** of a conductor is **directly proportional** to its **length**. If the length increases, the electrons encounter more collisions, increasing the resistance.
 
• **Cross-sectional Area (A):** The **resistance** is **inversely proportional** to the **area of cross-section**. A thicker wire (larger area) provides a wider path for electron flow, reducing resistance.
 
• **Nature of Material:** Different materials offer different levels of opposition to current flow, characterized by their **resistivity (ρ)**. Conductors like **Copper** and **Silver** have low resistivity.
 
• **Temperature:** For most metallic conductors, **resistance increases** with an **increase in temperature** due to more frequent atomic vibrations obstructing electron flow.
 
 
 
• **Resistivity (ρ):**
 
 
• It is the **resistance** offered by a wire of **unit length** and **unit cross-sectional area**.
 
• The **SI unit** of **resistivity** is **Ohm-meter (Ω" id="MathJax-Element-545-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">ΩΩ
 \Omega
 ⋅" id="MathJax-Element-546-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">⋅⋅
 \cdot
 m)**.
 
• Unlike resistance, **resistivity** does not change with the dimensions (length or area) of the wire; it only changes with the **material** and **temperature**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ohm’s Law:** This fundamental law states that the **current (I)** flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the **potential difference (V)** across its ends, provided physical conditions like temperature remain constant (**V = IR**).
 
• **SI Unit of Resistance:** The standard unit is the **Ohm (Ω" id="MathJax-Element-547-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">ΩΩ
 \Omega
 )**, named after the German physicist **Georg Simon Ohm**.
 
• **Practical Application:** In household wiring, thicker wires are used for high-power appliances (like air conditioners) because their **larger cross-sectional area** results in **lower resistance**, preventing the wires from overheating.
 
• **Calculation Summary:** When the **length** is **divided by 3** and the **area** is **multiplied by 2**, the total resistance becomes **1/6th** of the original value (**1/3 × 1/2 = 1/6**).

questions.question: What is the percentage of having a male child if the sex chromosomes of the father are XY and those of the mother are XX?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**50%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In humans, the sex of an individual is determined by a specific pair of **chromosomes** known as **sex chromosomes** or **allosomes**. Humans have a total of **23 pairs** of chromosomes, out of which **22 pairs** are **autosomes** and the **23rd pair** determines the sex.
 
• Females possess two identical sex chromosomes, denoted as **XX**. Because they only carry X chromosomes, all the **eggs** or **ova** produced by a female will contain one **X chromosome**. This condition is referred to as being **homogametic**.
 
• Males possess two different sex chromosomes, denoted as **XY**. During the process of **meiosis** (gamete formation), males produce two types of **sperm**: approximately **50%** carry the **X chromosome** and the other **50%** carry the **Y chromosome**. This makes males **heterogametic**.
 
• The sex of the **child** is determined at the moment of **fertilization** by the type of sperm that fuses with the egg. If a sperm carrying an **X chromosome** fertilizes the egg (X), the zygote becomes **XX**, resulting in a **female child**.
 
• If a sperm carrying a **Y chromosome** fertilizes the egg (X), the zygote becomes **XY**, resulting in a **male child**. Since the ratio of X-carrying sperm to Y-carrying sperm is **1:1**, the mathematical probability or **percentage** of having a male child is exactly **50%**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The SRY Gene**: The **Y chromosome** is significantly smaller than the **X chromosome** and carries a crucial gene called **SRY** (Sex-determining Region Y). This gene triggers the development of male characteristics in the **embryo**. In its absence, the embryo develops as a female.
 
• **Heterogamy vs. Homogamy**: In the **XY sex-determination system**, the male is the **heterogametic sex** (XY) and the female is the **homogametic sex** (XX). This system is prevalent in most **mammals** and some **insects** like **Drosophila**.
 
• **Punnett Square Analysis**: When crossing a mother (**XX**) and a father (**XY**), the possible combinations are **XX, XX, XY, and XY**. This clearly illustrates that **two out of four** possibilities result in a male, which equates to a **50%** frequency.
 
• **Other Systems**: It is important to note that not all species follow the XY system. For example, in **birds** and some **reptiles**, the **ZW system** is used where the **female** is the heterogametic sex (**ZW**) and the **male** is homogametic (**ZZ**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Scientific Responsibility**: In many societies, women are traditionally blamed for the sex of the child. However, biological evidence confirms that the **sex of the baby** is determined solely by the **genetic contribution of the father**, as only he can provide the **Y chromosome**.
 
• **Historical Context**: The role of **chromosomes** in sex determination was first identified in the early **20th century** (around **1905**) by scientists like **Nettie Stevens** and **Edmund Beecher Wilson**, who independently discovered the **XY** and **XO** systems.
 
• **Statistical Reality**: While the theoretical probability is **50%**, global **demographic data** often shows a slight natural skew (approximately **105 males to 100 females**) due to various biological factors influencing sperm motility or embryo survival, though the genetic chance remains **1 in 2**.

questions.question: In human beings, how is the sex of a child determined?

options.text: By the difference in number of chromosomes inherited by the child
By the inheritance of X or Y chromosome from the father
By the environmental conditions prevailing during development of the foetus
By the inheritance of an X chromosome from the mother

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**By the inheritance of X or Y chromosome from the father**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In human beings, every cell contains **23 pairs** of chromosomes, making a total of **46** chromosomes. Out of these, **22 pairs** are called **autosomes** and are identical in both males and females.
 
• The **23rd pair** of chromosomes is known as the **sex chromosome**, which differs between the two sexes. Females possess two **X chromosomes (XX)**, while males possess one **X** and one **Y chromosome (XY)**.
 
• During the process of **gametogenesis**, the mother produces **eggs (ova)** that always carry a single **X chromosome**. Therefore, the maternal contribution to the child's sex is always the same.
 
• The **father** produces two types of **sperm**: approximately **50%** carry an **X chromosome** and the other **50%** carry a **Y chromosome**.
 
• The sex of the child is determined at the moment of **fertilization**. If a sperm carrying an **X chromosome** fertilizes the egg, the resulting **zygote** will be **XX**, developing into a **female**. If a sperm carrying a **Y chromosome** fertilizes the egg, the **zygote** will be **XY**, developing into a **male**. ***Hence, statement 2 is the correct mechanism.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Heterogametic Sex:** In humans, the **male** is the **heterogametic sex** because he produces two different types of gametes (X and Y), whereas the female is **homogametic** as she produces only one type (X).
 
• **The SRY Gene:** The **Sex-determining Region Y (SRY)** gene, located on the **Y chromosome**, is the master switch that triggers the development of male physical characteristics. In the absence of this gene, the embryo develops into a female.
 
• **Probability of Sex:** Statistically, there is a **50:50 chance** of having a boy or a girl in each pregnancy, as the segregation of **X** and **Y** chromosomes into sperm occurs randomly during **meiosis**.
 
• **Genetic vs. Environmental Determination:** Unlike some reptiles (such as **crocodiles** and **turtles**) where the **incubation temperature** of the eggs determines the sex, human sex determination is strictly **genetic** and is not influenced by **environmental conditions** during the development of the **foetus**.
 
• **Chromosomal Abnormalities:** Sometimes, errors in cell division can lead to variations in the **23rd pair**, such as **Turner syndrome (XO)** or **Klinefelter syndrome (XXY)**, which affect physical and reproductive development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mendelian Inheritance:** The inheritance of sex follows **Mendel’s laws** of segregation, where alleles (in this case, sex chromosomes) separate during gamete formation.
 
• **Historical Context:** The discovery of the **XY sex-determination system** was made by **Nettie Stevens** and **Edmund Beecher Wilson** independently in **1905**.
 
• **Misconceptions:** It is a common biological fact that the **mother** does not determine the sex of the child; however, in many cultures, women have been historically blamed for not giving birth to a male child despite the **biological determination** coming from the **paternal sperm**.

questions.question: Work done by a constant force depends on which of the following?

options.text: Both force and displacement, and the angle between them

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both force and displacement, and the angle between them**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Work done** by a constant **force** is defined as the product of the magnitude of the **force**, the magnitude of the **displacement**, and the cosine of the **angle** between the force and the displacement vectors.
 
• The mathematical expression for work is **W = Fs cos θ**, where **W** is the work done, **F** is the constant **force**, **s** is the **displacement**, and **θ** is the **angle** between the force vector and the displacement vector.
 
• It depends on the **magnitude of force**: If the force applied is doubled while keeping other factors constant, the **work done** will also double. ***Hence, option 3 is only a partial factor.***
 
• It depends on the **displacement**: If an object does not move (**s = 0**), no work is done, regardless of how much force is applied. An example is pushing against a stationary **brick wall**. ***Hence, option 1 is also only a partial factor.***
 
• It depends on the **angle (θ)**: The direction of the force relative to the motion is crucial. If the force is **perpendicular** to the displacement (**θ = 90°**), the work done is **zero** because **cos 90° = 0**.
 
• **Mass** is not a direct variable in the basic formula for work done by a constant force, although it may influence the force required to move an object (via **F = ma**). ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Both force and displacement, and the angle between them.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Work:**

 
 
• **Positive Work:** Occurs when the **angle θ** is between **0° and 90°**. In this case, the force has a component in the direction of the displacement. An example is **lifting an object** upwards where the applied force is in the direction of movement.
 
• **Negative Work:** Occurs when the **angle θ** is between **90° and 180°**. The force acts in a direction opposite to the displacement. **Frictional force** doing work on a sliding block is a classic example of negative work.
 
• **Zero Work:** Occurs when the force is **perpendicular** to displacement or either force or displacement is **zero**. A **coolie** carrying a load on his head and walking on a horizontal platform does **zero work against gravity** because the force of gravity is vertical while the displacement is horizontal.
 
 
 
• **Units and Dimensions:**
 
 
• The **SI unit** of work is the **Joule (J)**. **1 Joule** is defined as the work done by a force of **1 Newton** causing a displacement of **1 meter**.
 
• In the **CGS system**, the unit of work is the **Erg**. The relationship between them is **1 Joule = 10⁷ Ergs**.
 
• The **dimensional formula** for work is **[ML²T⁻²]**, which is the same as that for **energy** and **torque**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Scalar Quantity:** Even though **force** and **displacement** are **vector quantities**, their dot product, **Work**, is a **scalar quantity**. This means it only has magnitude and no specific direction in space.
 
• **Work-Energy Theorem:** This theorem states that the **net work done** on an object is equal to the change in its **Kinetic Energy (KE)**. This connects the concept of work directly to the **velocity** and **mass** of the object.
 
• **External vs Internal Force:** The calculation of work depends on the specific force being considered. For example, while **gravity** does work on a falling apple, **air resistance** simultaneously does negative work on it.

questions.question: What term describes the rapid to and fro motion of an object that is essential for producing sound?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vibration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vibration** is defined as the **rapid to-and-fro or back-and-forth motion** of an object about its mean position. This mechanical motion is the fundamental requirement for the **production of sound**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Vibration.***
 
• Every source of sound, whether it is a **musical instrument** like a **guitar string**, a **tuning fork**, or the **human vocal cords**, must undergo **vibration** to generate pressure waves in the surrounding medium.
 
• When an object **vibrates**, it transfers its **energy** to the particles of the **medium** (solid, liquid, or gas) surrounding it. These particles then start vibrating, which leads to the **propagation** of sound waves.
 
• The **frequency** of these vibrations determines the **pitch** of the sound produced. A higher frequency of vibration results in a **high-pitched sound**, while a lower frequency results in a **low-pitched sound**.
 
• The **amplitude** of the vibration determines the **loudness** or **intensity** of the sound. Larger vibrations (greater displacement from the mean position) produce **louder sounds**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Compression**:

 
 
• In a **longitudinal wave** (like sound), **compression** is the region where the particles of the medium are **crowded together**.
 
• This region is characterized by **high pressure** and **high density**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect*** as it describes a state of the medium, not the motion of the source.
 
 
 
• **Rarefaction**:
 
 
• **Rarefaction** is the region in a longitudinal wave where the particles are **spread apart**.
 
• This area exhibits **low pressure** and **low density**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect*** because it refers to the wave's structure rather than the initiating motion.
 
 
 
• **Refraction**:
 
 
• **Refraction** is a phenomenon where a wave **changes direction** (bends) as it passes from one medium to another with a different **optical or acoustic density**.
 
• It occurs due to a change in the **speed** of the wave. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect*** as it relates to wave behavior at boundaries, not sound production.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Sound Waves**:
 
 
• Sound waves are **mechanical waves** and require a **material medium** for travel. They cannot propagate through a **vacuum**.
 
• The **speed of sound** in **dry air** at **20 degrees Celsius** (68 degrees Fahrenheit) is approximately **343 meters per second**.
 
• Sound travels fastest in **solids** (e.g., steel at approx **5960 m/s**), followed by **liquids** (e.g., water), and slowest in **gases**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Human Audibility**: The range of **audible frequencies** for the human ear is typically between **20 Hz and 20,000 Hz** (20 kHz).
 
• **Infrasound**: Frequencies below **20 Hz** are known as **infrasonic** sounds, often produced by **earthquakes** or **whales**.
 
• **Ultrasound**: Frequencies above **20,000 Hz** are called **ultrasonic** sounds, used in **medical imaging (sonography)** and by **bats** for navigation.
 
• **Oscillation**: While often used interchangeably with vibration, **oscillation** usually refers to slower, more rhythmic back-and-forth movements (like a **pendulum**), whereas **vibration** implies a more **rapid** movement.
 
• **Echo**: The **reflection** of sound arriving at the listener with a delay after the direct sound is known as an **echo**. To hear a distinct echo, the minimum distance from the reflecting surface should be approximately **17.2 meters**.
