questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding indicator?

a. Turmeric is a natural indicator used for acid base titration.

b. Phenopthalein is colourless in basic medium and gives pink colour in acidic medium.

c. Clove oil is categorised as olfactory indicator.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a and c**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indicators** are substances that change their color or odor when added to an acidic or basic solution. They are essential in **acid-base titration** to determine the endpoint of a reaction.
 
• **Turmeric** is a well-known **natural indicator**. It contains **curcumin**, which remains **yellow** in **acidic** and **neutral** environments but changes its color to **reddish-brown** when it comes into contact with a **base** (such as soap or sodium hydroxide). ***Hence, statement a is correct.***
 
• **Phenolphthalein** is a **synthetic indicator** often used in laboratories. It remains **colourless** in **acidic** and **neutral** solutions. However, it turns **pink** or **magenta** in a **basic medium** once the **pH** level exceeds approximately **8.2**. The statement provided reverses these characteristics. ***Hence, statement b is incorrect.***
 
• **Olfactory indicators** are specific substances whose **smell** changes in **acidic** or **basic** media. This property allows individuals, including those with visual impairments, to identify the nature of a solution. **Clove oil** is a classic example of an **olfactory indicator**, along with **onion** and **vanilla essence**. ***Hence, statement c is correct.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is a and c.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Indicators:**

 
 
• **Natural Indicators:** These are obtained from natural sources like plants. Examples include **Litmus** (extracted from **Lichens**), **Red Cabbage** extract, and **Turmeric**. **Litmus** turns **red** in **acid** and **blue** in **base**.
 
• **Synthetic Indicators:** These are man-made chemicals. **Methyl orange** and **Phenolphthalein** are the most common. **Methyl orange** gives a **red** color in **acidic** solutions and a **yellow** color in **basic** solutions.
 
• **Olfactory Indicators:** These work based on **odor**. In a **basic medium**, the characteristic **smell** of **onion** or **clove oil** is generally destroyed, while it persists in an **acidic medium**.
 
 
 
• **Uses and Applications:**
 
 
• **Titration:** Indicators are used to find the **equivalence point** where the **acid** and **base** have neutralized each other.
 
• **Soil Testing:** Farmers use indicators to check the **pH** of the **soil** to ensure optimal growth for specific crops.
 
• **Water Treatment:** Testing the **alkalinity** or **acidity** of water in swimming pools or industrial effluents.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Universal Indicator:** Unlike simple indicators, a **Universal Indicator** is a mixture of several indicators. It shows different colors at different **concentrations** of **hydrogen ions** (pH scale from **0 to 14**).
 
• **Clove Oil Specifics:** In the presence of **hydrochloric acid** (acid), the **smell** of **clove oil** is retained, but when mixed with **sodium hydroxide** (base), the **smell** cannot be detected.
 
• **Phenolphthalein Range:** It is widely used because its color transition is very sharp and occurs near the **neutralization point** for **strong acid-strong base** titrations.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of complex permanent tissue?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phloem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Complex permanent tissue** is defined as a collection of different types of cells that work together as a single unit to perform a common specialized function.
 
• **Phloem** is a prime example of complex permanent tissue because it consists of four distinct types of cells: **sieve tubes**, **companion cells**, **phloem parenchyma**, and **phloem fibers**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The primary function of **Phloem** is the **translocation** of soluble organic compounds, specifically **sucrose**, from the leaves (the source) to the roots and other storage organs (the sink).
 
• Unlike simple tissues, complex tissues like **Phloem** and **Xylem** are vital for the survival of **vascular plants** as they facilitate the long-distance transport of nutrients and water.
 
• **Lateral meristem** is not a permanent tissue; it is a type of **meristematic tissue** responsible for the **secondary growth** (increase in diameter) of the plant stem and roots. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Aerenchyma** is a specialized type of **simple permanent tissue** (a variation of **parenchyma**) that contains large air cavities, providing **buoyancy** to aquatic plants. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Collenchyma** is a **simple permanent tissue** composed of living cells with unevenly thickened walls (due to **cellulose** and **pectin**) that provide mechanical support and flexibility. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Xylem:**

 
 
• Along with phloem, **Xylem** is the second type of **complex permanent tissue** in plants.
 
• It is responsible for the conduction of **water and minerals** from the roots to the aerial parts of the plant.
 
• It consists of four elements: **tracheids**, **vessels**, **xylem parenchyma**, and **xylem fibers**.
 
• Except for **xylem parenchyma**, all other xylem cells are **dead** at maturity.
 
 
 
• **Simple Permanent Tissue:**
 
 
• These tissues are made up of only one type of cell which are similar in structure and function.
 
• **Parenchyma**: The most common tissue, involved in **photosynthesis**, storage, and secretion.
 
• **Sclerenchyma**: Consists of long, narrow cells with thick **lignified** walls; it provides structural strength and is usually **dead**.
 
 
 
• **Vascular Bundles:**
 
 
• In plants, **Xylem** and **Phloem** are organized into **vascular bundles**, which act as the plumbing system of the plant.
 
• The arrangement of these bundles varies between **monocots** and **dicots**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Direction of Flow**: In **Xylem**, the transport is strictly **unidirectional** (upwards from roots), whereas in **Phloem**, the transport is **bidirectional** (multi-directional) to ensure nutrients reach all parts of the plant.
 
• **Companion Cells**: These are specialized parenchyma cells in the **Phloem** that help regulate the metabolic activities of **sieve tube elements**, which lack a nucleus at maturity.
 
• **Sieve Plates**: The end walls of **sieve tube** cells have pores and are called **sieve plates**, allowing the flow of **cytoplasmic strands** between adjacent cells.
 
• **Secondary Growth**: The **Lateral meristems**, specifically the **vascular cambium**, produce new layers of secondary **Xylem** and secondary **Phloem** every year in woody plants.

questions.question: Which of the following is a typical physical property of non-metals?

options.text: They are brittle and poor conductors of electricity.
They conduct heat and electricity well.
They are ductile and shiny like metals.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They are brittle and poor conductors of electricity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Non-metals** are elements that do not possess the properties of metals, such as being able to conduct electricity or heat, or being **malleable** or **ductile**.
 
• One of the most defining physical properties of solid non-metals is **brittleness**. Unlike metals, which can be hammered into thin sheets, solid non-metals like **Sulfur** and **Phosphorus** will shatter or break into pieces when struck. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• Non-metals are generally **poor conductors** of **heat** and **electricity**. This is because, unlike metals, they do not have a "sea of free electrons" available to carry thermal energy or electric charge. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Properties like being **malleable** (capable of being beaten into sheets) and **sonorous** (producing a ringing sound when hit) are characteristic of **metals**, not non-metals. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Non-metals lack **metallic lustre**; they are usually dull in appearance and cannot be drawn into wires (**ductility**). ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• In the **Periodic Table**, non-metals are primarily located on the **right-hand side**, specifically within groups **14, 15, 16, 17, and 18**, with the exception of **Hydrogen**, which is placed in Group 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Physical States:** Non-metals can exist in all three states of matter at **room temperature**. For example, **Carbon** and **Sulfur** are **solids**, **Bromine** is a **liquid**, and **Oxygen** and **Nitrogen** are **gases**.
 
• **Bromine:** It is the only non-metal that remains in a **liquid** state at standard room temperature and pressure. It is a reddish-brown liquid with a suffocating odor.
 
• **Exceptions to Conductivity:** While most non-metals are insulators, **Graphite** (an allotrope of **Carbon**) is an excellent **conductor of electricity** due to its unique layered structure that allows electron mobility.
 
• **Exceptions to Hardness and Lustre:** **Diamond**, another allotrope of **Carbon**, is the **hardest natural substance** known on Earth. Furthermore, while non-metals are usually dull, **Iodine** crystals exhibit a distinct **metallic-like lustre** (shininess).
 
• **Density and Melting Points:** Generally, non-metals have **low densities** and **low melting and boiling points** compared to metals, making them less dense and more easily vaporized.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chemical Properties:** Non-metals are **electronegative** in nature. They tend to **gain electrons** during chemical reactions to form **anions** (negatively charged ions).
 
• **Nature of Oxides:** When non-metals react with **Oxygen**, they typically form **acidic oxides** (like **CO2** or **SO2**) or **neutral oxides** (like **N2O** or **CO**). This contrasts with metals, which usually form basic oxides.
 
• **Common Examples and Uses:**
 
 
• **Hydrogen:** Used in the manufacture of **ammonia** and as **rocket fuel**.
 
• **Oxygen:** Essential for **respiration** and **combustion** processes.
 
• **Nitrogen:** Used to provide an inert atmosphere and in the production of **fertilizers**.
 
• **Chlorine:** Widely used for **water purification** and as a bleaching agent.
 
• **Silicon:** A **metalloid** (sharing some non-metal properties) used extensively in the **semiconductor** industry for making microchips.
 
 
 
• **Valence Electrons:** Most non-metals have **4 to 8 electrons** in their outermost shell, which determines their high ionization energy and chemical reactivity.

questions.question: Which of the following glands add their secretions to make easier transport and to provide nutrition for sperms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prostate and seminal vesicles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **male reproductive system** consists of various accessory glands, primarily the **seminal vesicles**, the **prostate gland**, and the **bulbourethral glands**.
 
• These glands play a crucial role in reproduction by secreting fluids that combine with **sperms** to form **semen**. These secretions are collectively known as **seminal plasma**.
 
• The **seminal vesicles** secrete a significant portion of the fluid that contains **fructose**, which serves as the primary **nutrition** and energy source for **sperm** motility. *Hence, the role of seminal vesicles in nutrition is vital.*
 
• The **prostate gland** contributes a milky, slightly **alkaline fluid** that contains enzymes and **citric acid**. This fluid helps in the **transport** of sperm and enhances their **motility** while neutralizing the acidic environment of the female reproductive tract. *Hence, the prostate gland is essential for easier transport.*
 
• Since both the **prostate** and **seminal vesicles** contribute to these specific functions of nutrition and transport, the combined option is the most accurate. *Hence, the correct answer is Prostate and seminal vesicles.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Seminal Vesicles**:

 
 
• These are a pair of simple tubular glands located behind the **urinary bladder** in **males**.
 
• They produce approximately **60% to 70%** of the total volume of **semen**.
 
• The fluid is rich in **proteins**, **enzymes**, **fructose**, **vitamin C**, and **prostaglandins**. The **prostaglandins** help in the movement of sperm by inducing contractions in the female reproductive tract.
 
 
 
• **Prostate Gland**:
 
 
• It is a single, walnut-sized gland located just below the **bladder** and surrounds the **urethra**.
 
• It secretes a thin, milky fluid that makes up about **20% to 30%** of the **semen**.
 
• Its **alkaline** nature protects the **sperms** from the **acidic** nature of the male **urethra** and the female **vagina**, ensuring their **survival**.
 
 
 
• **Bulbourethral Glands (Cowper's Glands)**:
 
 
• These are small, pea-sized glands located inferior to the **prostate gland**.
 
• They secrete an **alkaline mucus** during sexual arousal that **lubricates** the **penis** and neutralizes any **acidic urine** remaining in the **urethra**.
 
 
 
• **Pineal Gland**:
 
 
• Unlike the reproductive glands, the **Pineal gland** is an **endocrine gland** located in the **epithalamus** of the **brain**.
 
• It is responsible for secreting the hormone **melatonin**, which regulates the body's **circadian rhythm** and **sleep-wake cycles**. It has no direct involvement in **sperm** transport or **nutrition**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Semen Composition**: **Semen** is a mixture of **sperms** (produced in the **testes**) and **seminal plasma** (the collective secretions of the accessory glands).
 
• **Fructose**: It is an important forensic marker because it is produced only by the **seminal vesicles** and is not found elsewhere in the body's secretions.
 
• **Sperm Motility**: Without the secretions from the **prostate** and **seminal vesicles**, **sperms** would lack the energy and the fluid medium necessary to reach the **egg** for **fertilization**.

questions.question: What is the chemical reaction involved in the preparation of Plaster of Paris from gypsum?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CaSO4 . 2H2O + heat -> CaSO4 . 1/2H2O + 1 1/2H2O**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plaster of Paris** (**POP**) is chemically known as **Calcium Sulphate Hemihydrate**. Its chemical formula is **CaSO4 . 1/2H2O**.
 
• It is prepared from **Gypsum**, which is **Calcium Sulphate Dihydrate** (**CaSO4 . 2H2O**).
 
• The preparation involves heating **Gypsum** at a carefully controlled temperature of **373 K** (which equals **100 degrees Celsius**).
 
• At this temperature, **Gypsum** loses **one and a half molecules** (or **three-fourths**) of its **water of crystallization** to become the **hemihydrate** form. ***Hence, option 3 is correct.***
 
• In the chemical reaction **CaSO4 . 2H2O + heat -> CaSO4 . 1/2H2O + 1 1/2H2O**, the reactant is **Gypsum** and the product is **Plaster of Paris**.
 
• Option 1 represents the **setting process** where **Plaster of Paris** reacts with **water** to turn back into hard **Gypsum**. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Option 2 shows the **total dehydration** of **Gypsum** which occurs when it is heated strongly above **373 K**, resulting in **dead burnt plaster**. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Option 4 shows the **thermal decomposition** of **Calcium Carbonate** (**Limestone**) into **Calcium Oxide** (**Quicklime**) and **Carbon Dioxide**. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Origin of Name**: It is called **Plaster of Paris** because **Gypsum** was found in abundance in the **Montmartre** district of **Paris**, where it was first used for architectural purposes on a large scale.
 
• **Medical Uses**: One of the most common **applications** of **POP** is in **orthopedics**. Doctors use it as a **bandage** or **cast** to support and immobilize **fractured bones**, ensuring they heal in the correct **location** and alignment.
 
• **Dead Burnt Plaster**: If **Gypsum** is heated to a temperature higher than **373 K**, all the **water of crystallization** is removed. The resulting **Anhydrous Calcium Sulphate** (**CaSO4**) does not set like **POP** when mixed with **water** and is termed **dead burnt plaster**.
 
• **Physical Properties**: **Plaster of Paris** is a **white powder**. A unique **feature** is its ability to expand slightly upon **setting**, which makes it excellent for **casting** molds as it picks up the fine details of the **cast**.
 
• **Artistic and Industrial Uses**: Apart from construction, it is used for making **statues**, **toys**, **cheap ornaments**, and **blackboard chalk**. In **dentistry**, it is used to make **impressions** of teeth.
 
• **Chemical Detail**: In the formula **CaSO4 . 1/2H2O**, it is understood that **two formula units** of **CaSO4** share **one molecule** of **water** (**2CaSO4 . H2O**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Storage**: **Plaster of Paris** should be stored in **moisture-proof containers** because it absorbs moisture from the air and undergoes **hydration** to form a hard mass of **Gypsum**, rendering it useless.
 
• **Reaction Temperature**: Temperature control is **vital**. If the temperature is not maintained at exactly **373 K**, the quality and **setting properties** of the **plaster** are compromised.
 
• **Water Ratio**: When mixing **POP** for use, the **water-to-powder ratio** determines the **strength** and **setting time** of the final product.

questions.question: Which of the polyatomic ion has ‘n’ value equal to 3?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PO4-n**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **polyatomic ion**, also known as a molecular ion, is a charged chemical species composed of two or more atoms covalently bonded that act as a single unit. The **"n" value** in the context of these ions refers to the **magnitude of the ionic charge**.
 
• **PO4-n (Phosphate Ion)**: The phosphate ion consists of one **phosphorus** atom surrounded by four **oxygen** atoms in a tetrahedral arrangement. Its chemical formula is **PO4 3-**. Therefore, the value of **n** is **3**. ***Hence, this statement is correct.***
 
• **SO4-n (Sulfate Ion)**: The sulfate ion is a polyatomic anion consisting of one **sulfur** atom and four **oxygen** atoms. The standard charge for a sulfate ion is **-2**, which means the **n** value is **2**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **CO3-n (Carbonate Ion)**: The carbonate ion is composed of one **carbon** atom and three **oxygen** atoms. It carries a net charge of **-2**, making the **n** value equal to **2**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **HCO3-n (Bicarbonate Ion)**: Also known as the **hydrogen carbonate** ion, it consists of one **hydrogen**, one **carbon**, and three **oxygen** atoms. It carries a charge of **-1**, meaning the **n** value is **1**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Phosphate Ion (PO4 3-)**:

 
 
• This ion is **trivalent**, meaning it has a valency of **3**.
 
• It is a vital component in **biological systems**, forming the backbone of **DNA** and **RNA**.
 
• It is also a key part of **ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate)**, which is the primary **energy currency** of the cell.
 
• In agriculture, phosphates are used extensively in **fertilizers** to promote plant growth.
 
 
 
• **Sulfate Ion (SO4 2-)**:
 
 
• Sulfates are widely used in the **chemical industry** and are found in common substances like **Epsom salts (Magnesium sulfate)** and **Gypsum (Calcium sulfate)**.
 
• In environmental science, atmospheric sulfates are major contributors to **acid rain**.
 
 
 
• **Carbonate (CO3 2-) and Bicarbonate (HCO3 -) Ions**:
 
 
• **Carbonates** are found in minerals like **Calcite** and are the primary component of **limestone** and **shells** of marine organisms.
 
• **Bicarbonate** plays a crucial role in the **human body** as a **buffer system**, helping to maintain the **pH balance** of **blood** (keeping it around **7.4**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The charge of a polyatomic ion is the result of the total number of **electrons** being different from the total number of **protons** in the combined group of atoms.
 
• Most polyatomic ions are **oxyanions**, which are polyatomic ions that contain **oxygen**. Examples include **Nitrate (NO3 -)**, **Nitrite (NO2 -)**, and **Sulfite (SO3 2-)**.
 
• **Valency vs. Charge**: While valency refers to the **combining capacity** of an element or ion, the charge (n) indicates the **actual electrical state**. For the ions mentioned, the magnitude of the charge matches the common valency.
 
• **Ammonium (NH4 +)** is one of the few common **positively charged** (cationic) polyatomic ions, with an **n** value of **1**.

questions.question: If each of the length, breadth and height of a cuboid is doubled, its total surface area becomes ________ the original total surface area.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If all linear dimensions of a 3D object are multiplied by a scale factor *k*, its surface area becomes *k*² times.

Here, all dimensions (length, breadth, and height) are doubled, so the scale factor *k* = 2.

New Total Surface Area = 2² = 4 times the original area.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 times.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let the original dimensions of the cuboid be length = l, breadth = b, and height = h.

The new dimensions after doubling are length = 2l, breadth = 2b, and height = 2h.

**Formula Used:**

Total Surface Area of a cuboid = 2(lb + bh + hl)

 
 
 l h b 
• 
 Doubled 
 
 2l 2h 2b Original Area New Area = 4 × Original 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Original Total Surface Area = 2(lb + bh + hl)

⇒ New Total Surface Area = 2 × [(2l × 2b) + (2b × 2h) + (2h × 2l)]

⇒ New Total Surface Area = 2 × [4lb + 4bh + 4hl]

⇒ New Total Surface Area = 4 × 2(lb + bh + hl)

⇒ New Total Surface Area = 4 × Original Total Surface Area

**∴ The correct answer is 4 times.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Scaling Factor in Mensuration

When linear dimensions of any shape are scaled by a factor 'k', its total surface area scales by k², and its volume scales by k³.

Cuboid Formulas

Volume = l × b × h | Lateral Surface Area = 2h(l + b) | Length of Diagonal = √(l² + b² + h²).

Cube Formulas

For a cube of side 'a', Volume = a³ | Total Surface Area = 6a² | Lateral Surface Area = 4a².

questions.question: If 20% of a number is added to 72, then the result is the same number. 70% of the same number is:

x = 90

= 63

**∴ Answer = 63**

20% of a number + 72 = the number

Percentage = value/100 × number

⇒ 0.2x + 72 = x

⇒ x − 0.2x = 72

⇒ 0.8x = 72

⇒ x = 90

questions.question: The arithmetic mean of the observations 61, 33, 94, 48, 36, 93, 73, 94 and 53 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the assumed mean be 60.

Net deviation from 60 = (+1) + (−27) + (+34) + (−12) + (−24) + (+33) + (+13) + (+34) + (−7) = +45

Average deviation = +45 ÷ 9 = +5

Actual Mean = Assumed Mean + Average deviation = 60 + 5 = 65

**∴ The correct answer is 65.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Observations: 61, 33, 94, 48, 36, 93, 73, 94, 53

Number of observations (n) = 9

**Formula Used:**

Arithmetic Mean = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Number of observations)

 
• 
• Mean = 65 61 33 94 48 36 93 73 94 53 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of observations = 61 + 33 + 94 + 48 + 36 + 93 + 73 + 94 + 53

⇒ Sum of observations = 585

⇒ Mean = 585 ÷ 9

⇒ Mean = 65

**∴ The correct answer is 65.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

It is the sum of a collection of numbers divided by the count of numbers in the collection. Formula: Mean = Sum of values ÷ Number of values.

Assumed Mean Method (Deviation Method)

This method simplifies calculations by assuming a central value as the mean and averaging the deviations from it. Formula: Actual Mean = Assumed Mean + (Sum of Deviations ÷ Number of Values).

Weighted Average

When different values have different frequencies or importance, the average is calculated as: Weighted Mean = (w₁x₁ + w₂x₂ + ... + wₙxₙ) ÷ (w₁ + w₂ + ... + wₙ).

Three non-zero quantities a, b, and c are in continued proportion if a : b = b : c. This implies the fundamental rule b² = a × c.
